chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about feeding ten poor people or feeding sixty poor people: is that gathered for one person to be given to him? He said, 'No, but he gives one person to another, as Allah the Exalted said.' I said, 'Does the man give to his relatives if they are needy?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Does he give to the weak from those outside the family of the Imam?' He said, 'Yes, and the family of the Imam are more beloved to me.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْوَلَايَةِ: The family of the Imam (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: How should the feeding of the poor be distributed for expiation or khums according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is made between consolidating fidya (expiation) for a single person versus distributing it among multiple poor, emphasizing the prophetic precedent of individual distribution. The Imam further clarifies that while giving to non-Ahl al-Bayt relatives is permissible, the Ahl al-Bayt are preferred, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing the Prophet's family in charitable distributions. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of Oaths and Vows, illustrating the practical application of Quranic verses on expiation.
